title: Case study: search autocomplete
summary: Keystroke-rate estimation, a precomputed top-K prefix index held in RAM, cacheable suggest API, decayed counts and sketches, immutable snapshots swapped atomically, safety filters, with a prefix-index lab.

units.title: Guided design: requirements, estimation, API, data model, high-level design
Deep dives: the prefix index, the freshness pipeline and snapshot publishing, the lab

labs.title: Prefix index with precomputed top-K, atomically swappable serving snapshot, half-life decaying counter

outcomes.text: Scope an autocomplete prompt in six minutes: ask the questions that change the design (volume, what is completed, personalisation, freshness, latency, K and prefix length, locales, what must never be suggested, behaviour when suggest is down), state NFRs as numbers and an explicit out-of-scope list.

Estimate keystroke-rate lookups (searches × keystrokes × peak, before and after client mitigation), index memory from distinct prefixes and bytes per node, serving nodes, egress, log volume and snapshot distribution, and tie each number to a decision, above all replicate-whole vs partition.

Design a cacheable suggest API (GET, normalised q echoed, empty list for an empty prefix, Cache-Control with stale-* directives, capped limit, edge rate limits), the client's debounce, prefix cache and sequencing, and the three data sets (raw events, aggregated counts, serving snapshot) with their keys and stores.

Draw the read path (client → CDN → load balancer → replicas holding the index in RAM) and the write path (submitted searches → log → aggregation → build → validate → versioned snapshot → canaried rollout), justify every box with a requirement or a number, and walk one keystroke through it against the latency budget.

Choose an index layout (trie with precomputed top-K ids, hash map of prefixes, sorted array + scan, FST) with lookup cost and bytes per node, explain why top-K at query time is backwards for a hot path, and explain how a pointer-free layout avoids garbage-collector pauses.

Design freshness: exponential decay with a half-life instead of resets or hard windows, exact batch counts for the main tier, a count-min sketch plus heavy hitters for a per-minute trending tier, and the lookup-time merge of the two.

Publish a new index with no lock on the read path: immutable versioned snapshots, validation and golden prefixes, atomic pointer swap, canary and waves within the 2× memory headroom, rollback; and handle hot prefixes and partitioning (locale, then split ranges or a hash ring, hot shards replicated more, shortest prefixes at the edge).

Keep suggestions safe: minimum support on distinct users rather than raw counts, a whole-word blocklist at build time, and a fast override set for takedowns applied at lookup over every tier, with an audit trail and a propagation SLO.

Implement in Go, passing tests under -race, a prefix index with a precomputed top-K per node, a serving snapshot swapped through an atomic pointer, and a lazily decaying counter whose snapshot feeds the next build (labs/c12/suggest).

Extend the design without touching the global path: client-side or parallel-endpoint personalisation, bounded fuzzy prefix matching with precomputed candidates, and multi-region serving from replicated snapshots.
